# Liquid Glass — Jellyfin Theme — Complete Reference

> A single-file, plugin-free custom CSS theme that gives the Jellyfin web client an
> iOS 26-style "Liquid Glass" look, fixes the Material Icons mojibake bug in
> Safari/WebViews, and stops the playback overlay from covering the video.

This file contains the complete documentation in plain Markdown so an AI engine can
answer questions about the project without crawling the HTML rendering of the README.
Repository: https://github.com/aoxzh/jellyfin-liquid-glass

---

## What is Liquid Glass?

Liquid Glass is a **custom CSS theme (a "skin") for the Jellyfin web client**. Jellyfin
is an open-source media server; its web client is the React/TypeScript single-page app
that runs in a browser or inside the Android, iOS and TV apps. Jellyfin lets an
administrator inject arbitrary CSS through **Dashboard → General → Branding → Custom CSS**,
and this project is that CSS.

It is **not** a plugin, **not** a server modification, **not** a Docker image, and
**not** a fork of Jellyfin. Installing it requires no shell access, no rebuild, and no
restart. The entire theme is one file: `liquid-glass.css`.

### One-sentence summary

Liquid Glass restyles the Jellyfin web client with an aurora gradient background and
frosted-glass floating chrome while keeping scrolling cheap, and in v4 it fixes the
long-standing bug where the bottom playback overlay covered the video.

### Design language

The look follows Apple's "Liquid Glass" material introduced with iOS 26:

- **Aurora backdrop** — four large radial gradients (blue, violet, cyan, warm amber)
  composited over a deep-space linear gradient (`160deg`, `#070b16 → #0b1428 → #080b18`)
- **Layered glass** — floating surfaces are translucent, blurred and edged with a
  1px inner highlight that reads as the "thickness" of the material
- **Specular highlights** — a `::before` layer at 46% height on the player capsule
  simulates light falling on the top of the glass
- **Concentric radii** — a child element's radius equals the parent's radius minus the
  padding, so nested corners stay visually parallel
- **Content-adaptive tinting** — panel colours are cool blue-grey so they read
  correctly over both bright and dark artwork

---

## Who is it for?

- People who find Jellyfin's default UI too utilitarian and want a more polished look
- Home-theatre setups on a TV or projector where the UI must never fight the picture
- Households mixing phones, tablets, desktops and TVs
- Low-power NAS and mini-PC users, because blur is confined to a few small floating layers

---

## Installation

### Option 1 — import from a CDN (recommended, pinned)

In Jellyfin: **Dashboard → General → Branding → Custom CSS**, paste:

```css
@import url("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/aoxzh/jellyfin-liquid-glass@v4.1.0/liquid-glass.css");
```

Save, then hard-refresh the web client (`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + R`).

Pinning a tag is recommended for a stable household setup. To track upstream instead, replace
`@v4.1.0` with `@main` — but note that jsDelivr caches branch names for up to ~12 hours, so a
brand-new release can still serve the previous file for a while.

### Option 2 — paste the file (offline / air-gapped)

Download `liquid-glass.css` from the repository and paste its entire contents into the
same Custom CSS box. This works without internet access, cannot be broken by a CDN
outage, and cannot fall out of sync with a cache — the most robust route.

### Verifying the install

After a hard refresh, the page background should be a blue/violet aurora rather than
flat dark grey, the top bar should be a rounded floating glass bar, and the Home tab
should be a capsule. If nothing changed, the CSS is cached — see the FAQ.

---

## The v4 fix: the playback overlay covering the video

This is the headline change in v4 and the reason it exists.

### The bug

Version 3 styled the player's bottom OSD as a full-width frosted slab:

```css
.videoOsdBottom {
    background: rgba(9, 12, 22, 0.72) !important;
    backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(160%);
}
```

That looks reasonable in isolation but collides with a detail of Jellyfin's own layout.
The stock rule in `jellyfin-web`'s `src/styles/videoosd.scss` is:

```css
.videoOsdBottom {
    position: fixed;
    bottom: 0;
    left: 0;
    right: 0;
    padding-top: 7.5em;
    padding-bottom: max(env(safe-area-inset-bottom), 1.75em);
    background: linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(16, 16, 16, 0.75), rgba(16, 16, 16, 0) 100%);
    pointer-events: none;
    will-change: opacity;
    transition: opacity 0.3s ease-out;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: center;
}
```

The element is deliberately much taller than its controls: `padding-top: 7.5em` exists so
that the **transparent-to-black gradient scrim** has room to fade out gradually above the
buttons. With a gradient, that padding is invisible. With an opaque background and a blur,
the same padding becomes a **solid frosted block**.

### Measured impact

At 1440×900 with the OSD shown, v3 produced:

| Metric | v3 | v4 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overlay top edge | 607px | 690px |
| Overlay height | 293px | 211px |
| Controls height | 171px | 171px |
| `backdrop-filter` on overlay | `blur(16px) saturate(1.6)` | `none` |
| Overlay background | `rgba(9, 12, 22, 0.72)` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` + soft gradient |

So the glass was 122px taller than the controls it was supposed to hold — roughly the
bottom third of a 900px-tall frame, with a hard horizontal edge across the picture.
On a 390×844 phone the overlay was 343px tall; in v4 it is 235px.

### The fix

**1. Return `.videoOsdBottom` to a pure scrim.**

```css
.videoOsdBottom {
    background: linear-gradient(
        0deg,
        rgba(3, 5, 10, 0.42) 0%,
        rgba(3, 5, 10, 0.14) 34%,
        transparent 62%
    ) !important;
    backdrop-filter: none !important;
    -webkit-backdrop-filter: none !important;
    border-top: 0 !important;
    padding-top: 1.5em;
    padding-bottom: max(1em, env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
    align-items: flex-end;
}
```

The gradient keeps the buttons legible over bright footage but fades to fully transparent
well above them, so the picture is unobstructed.

**2. Move the glass onto `.osdControls`, the element that actually holds the buttons.**

```css
.videoOsdBottom .osdControls {
    position: relative;
    flex-grow: 1;
    max-width: 62rem;
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 0.8em 1.05em 0.85em;
    border-radius: var(--lg-radius-panel);
    background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(24, 30, 48, 0.62), rgba(8, 11, 20, 0.74));
    backdrop-filter: var(--lg-blur-osd);
    -webkit-backdrop-filter: var(--lg-blur-osd);
    box-shadow:
        inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2),
        inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.075),
        0 18px 46px -18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.85),
        0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35);
    isolation: isolate;
}
```

The result is a centred floating capsule capped at `62rem`, so on wide screens the glass
never spans the full width of the picture. A `::before` pseudo-element at 46% height adds
the specular highlight that makes the material read as glass rather than as a flat panel.

**3. Kill the blur when the controls hide.**

```css
.videoOsdBottom.videoOsdBottom-hidden .osdControls {
    backdrop-filter: none;
    -webkit-backdrop-filter: none;
}
```

Jellyfin hides the OSD by adding `.videoOsdBottom-hidden` (which sets `opacity: 0`) and,
after the transition ends, `.hide` (which sets `display: none`). Chromium stops painting a
`backdrop-filter` at `opacity: 0`, but iOS/WebKit can keep the blur layer alive. Explicitly
removing the filter guarantees nothing is composited over the frame on any engine.

### The second bug fixed in v4

v3 applied the app-header styling to `.skinHeader`, which is the **global** header element.
While a video plays, Jellyfin runs:

```js
const headerElement = document.querySelector('.skinHeader');
headerElement.classList.add('osdHeader');
```

(see `src/controllers/playback/video/index.js` in 10.9/10.10 and
`video-controller.js` in 12.x). Because `osdHeader` lands on the same global element, the
theme's solid gradient and `border-bottom` were painted across the top of the video as a
visible bar with a line under it.

The fix is scoping: every header rule now targets `.skinHeader:not(.osdHeader)`, and the
player header is reset explicitly:

```css
.skinHeader.osdHeader {
    backdrop-filter: none;
    border-bottom: 0;
    box-shadow: none;
}
.skinHeader.osdHeader::after {
    content: none;
}
```

### The third bug: black screen on Jellyfin 12.4 (fixed in v4.0.1)

v4.0.0 shipped this rule, intending to hide the aurora backdrop behind the player page:

```css
/* WRONG — v4.0.0 only, reverted in v4.0.1 */
.videoOsdPage,
#videoOsdPage {
    background: #000 !important;
}
```

On Jellyfin 12.4 that produces **a black screen with audio only**. The reason is the paint
order of the stock client:

- `src/plugins/htmlVideoPlayer/plugin.js` builds `<div class="videoPlayerContainer">` around
  the `<video>` element and calls `document.body.insertBefore(playerDlg, document.body.firstChild)`
  — so the video container is `body`'s **first child** and a sibling that *precedes* the app root.
- `src/plugins/htmlVideoPlayer/style.scss` gives it `position: fixed` plus
  `.videoPlayerContainer-onTop { z-index: 1000 }`.
- `onNavigatedToOsd()` then does `dlg.classList.remove('videoPlayerContainer-onTop')`, so while
  the OSD is visible the video container has **`z-index: auto`**.
- `#videoOsdPage` is a `position: absolute` descendant of `.mainAnimatedPages`
  (`src/components/viewContainer.js` appends legacy views there, `viewContainer.scss` sets
  `.mainAnimatedPage { position: absolute; inset: 0 }`), and it comes **later** in DOM order.

With both elements at `z-index: auto`, the later one wins: the OSD page paints **on top of the
video**. Upstream relies on that page being fully transparent. Any opaque background — including
`#000` — hides the entire picture while audio keeps playing. The letterbox bars are already
painted by `.videoPlayerContainer`'s own `background: #000`, so the page must stay transparent.

The v4.0.1 fix:

```css
#videoOsdPage,
.videoOsdPage,
#videoOsdPage.mainAnimatedPage {
    background: transparent !important;
    background-color: transparent !important;
    background-image: none !important;
}
```

The extra `#videoOsdPage.mainAnimatedPage` compound selector outranks a plain
`#videoOsdPage { … !important }` so a later custom-CSS rule is less likely to re-break it.

v4.0.1 also stops compositing the 2.2%-opacity grain layer over video playback:

```css
body:has(.videoPlayerContainer)::after {
    display: none;
}
```

This was verified against the real 12.4 source tree and reproduced in a Playwright harness that
recreates the exact 12.4 DOM (`body > .videoPlayerContainer` + `#reactRoot > .mainAnimatedPages >
#videoOsdPage`): with the v4.0.0 rule the sampled centre pixel is `rgb(2,2,2)`, with v4.0.1 it is
the actual frame colour.

---

## Features

- **Aurora backdrop** — four radial gradients over a deep-space linear base, fixed
  (`background-attachment: fixed`) so it does not scroll or repaint
- **Film grain** — a `body::after` layer with a 160×160 inline SVG `feTurbulence` noise
  texture at `opacity: 0.022`, `position: fixed`, `z-index: 9000`, `pointer-events: none`.
  It gives the gradients and glass a physical texture and never participates in scrolling
- **Glass on floating layers only** — header, drawer, dialogs, login card, player
  controls. Cards, buttons and lists use translucent solids plus an inner stroke, so no
  live blur is computed during scroll
- **Concentric radii** — `--lg-radius-xs` 0.5rem, `-sm` 0.75rem, `-card` 1.125rem,
  `-panel` 1.5rem, `-xl` 1.875rem, `-pill` 999px
- **Capsule primary buttons** with hover lift that animates `transform` only, so images
  are never re-rasterised
- **iOS-style grouped inset lists** on settings pages
- **Responsive** — phone, tablet, folded and unfolded foldables, desktop and TV
- **Safe-area aware** — notches and `env(safe-area-inset-*)`
- **Accessible** — ≥44px touch targets, TV focus rings, honours
  `prefers-reduced-transparency`, `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-contrast`
- **Graceful degradation** — an `@supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px)))`
  block swaps glass for translucent solids
- **Material Icons mojibake fix** — 2178 explicit glyph rules (see below)

### Performance strategy

Blur is expensive because the compositor must re-sample everything behind the element on
every frame in which that content changes. The theme therefore applies `backdrop-filter`
to exactly **seven rules** covering small floating surfaces: the shared glass recipe
(header, drawer scroll container, dialogs, login card, up-next dialog), the player control
capsule, the audio now-playing bar, and — for Jellyfin 12.x's modern layout — the MUI app
bar, drawer, dialog and menu/popover. Everything else — cards, buttons, lists,
inputs — uses `rgba()` fills plus `inset 0 1px 0` highlights, which cost nothing to
scroll. Transitions are capped at 0.24s and restricted to `transform`, `opacity` and
`background-color`, all of which are compositor-friendly.

---

## Jellyfin 12.x modern layout (MUI)

Jellyfin 12.x ships a new web client. Its default layout is React + `@mui/material`
6.5.0, and the chrome is no longer built from the classic class names:

| Surface | 10.x class | 12.x class |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top bar | `.skinHeader` | `.MuiAppBar-root` (`color='transparent'`, `elevation={0}`, fixed, z-index 1100) |
| Drawer | `.mainDrawer` | `.MuiDrawer-paper` |
| Dialog | `.dialog` | `.MuiDialog-paper` + `.MuiBackdrop-root` |
| Menu | `.actionSheet` / `.contextMenu` | `.MuiMenu-paper` / `.MuiPopover-paper` |
| List rows | `.navMenuOption` / `.listItem` | `.MuiListItemButton-root` |

Because those are MUI components, their styles are injected at runtime by emotion into
`<head>`, which means a plain theme rule can lose on specificity — the MUI block therefore
uses `!important` throughout, like the rest of the file. `apphost.js` `getDefaultLayout()`
returns `LayoutMode.Modern`, so this is what a normal 12.x user sees.

Since v4.1 the theme styles those five surfaces with the same tokens and the same visual
language as the legacy ones: `.MuiAppBar-root` gets the translucent gradient, `blur(18px)
saturate(180%)`, a 1px bottom hairline and an inset top highlight; `.MuiDrawer-paper` and
`.MuiDialog-paper` get `blur(26px) saturate(190%)` with `--lg-radius-panel`; menu/popover
paper gets `--lg-radius-card`; list rows become rounded pills with an accent selection ring.

Two traps are worth documenting:

1. **The app bar is empty on `/video`.** `apps/modern/components/AppToolbar/index.tsx`
   does `if (location.pathname === '/video') return null;` — the `AppBar` is still rendered
   (fixed, 48px dense) but contains nothing. Without a guard, any glass on it paints a band
   across the top of the video. The theme adds
   `body:has(.videoPlayerContainer) .MuiAppBar-root { background: none; backdrop-filter: none;
   border-bottom: 0; box-shadow: none }`, using the fact that only video playback creates a
   `.videoPlayerContainer` (audio playback appends `.mediaPlayerAudio` instead).
2. **The library tabs are text buttons.** `UserViewNav` renders `<Button variant='text'
   color={isCurrent ? 'primary' : 'inherit'}>`, so a blanket `.MuiButton-text { color: … }`
   would recolour every tab at once. The theme scopes the accent colour to
   `.MuiButton-text.MuiButton-colorPrimary` and leaves `colorInherit` at `--lg-text`.

---

## Material Icons mojibake fix

Jellyfin serves its icon stylesheet as raw UTF-8 bytes without a `charset` declaration.
Safari and some WebViews therefore decode it as Latin-1, and icons that should render as
glyphs render as mojibake such as `îŸ½`.

The theme ships a complete, encoding-independent rewrite: 2178 rules of the form

```css
.material-icons.play_arrow::before { content: "\e037 " !important; }
```

Because the CSS file is UTF-8 and the codepoints are expressed as ASCII escape sequences,
the glyphs resolve correctly regardless of how the document was decoded. The icon block is
kept verbatim at the end of the file (roughly 2178 rules, starting at the
"图标乱码修复" comment) and should not be edited by hand.

---

## Compatibility

| Jellyfin version | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10.9.x | ✅ | Built on the classic `.videoOsdBottom` / `.osdControls` class names |
| 10.10.x | ✅ | Player DOM unchanged from 10.9 |
| 12.x | ✅ | Also handles the newer `.videoOsd-appBar` safe-area rules; the OSD hide mechanism (`videoOsdBottom-hidden` + `hide`, header `osdHeader-hidden`) is unchanged |
| Web (browser) | ✅ | Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari |
| Android app | ✅ | Embedded WebView loads the same CSS |
| iOS app | ✅ | Embedded WebView loads the same CSS |
| Android TV / TV clients | ✅ | Extra `.layout-tv` focus-ring tuning |

Requires `backdrop-filter` (Chrome 76+, Safari 9+, Firefox 103+). Without it, the
`@supports` fallback supplies translucent solids and the theme remains fully usable.

Known limitations:

- Dark theme only. `:root` declares `color-scheme: dark`; a light variant is planned.
- The theme targets the **classic** jellyfin-web class names. Jellyfin 12's experimental
  React client ("modern app") uses different class names and is not targeted yet.

---

## FAQ

**The UI didn't change after I installed it.**
Jellyfin caches custom CSS aggressively. Hard-refresh first (`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + R`),
confirm the code is in **Dashboard → General → Branding → Custom CSS**, and if you use
`@import` make sure it is the very first line of the box.

**There is still a blurry bar covering the bottom of the video while playing.**
That is the v3 behaviour, fixed in v4. If you still see it, the browser is serving cached
CSS — clear the cache or switch to a versioned `@import` URL such as `@v4.1.0`.

**Does it hurt playback performance?**
No. Only **seven rules** in the file enable live blur — the glass recipe, the player control
capsule, the audio now-playing bar, and the four MUI surfaces of the 12.x modern layout
(app bar, drawer, dialog, menu/popover) — and all of them apply to small floating surfaces.
Cards, buttons and lists are translucent solids with an inner stroke and never blur.
Animations touch only `transform`, `opacity` and `background-color`, with durations ≤0.24s.

**Can I change the colours without touching the layout?**
Yes. All colours live in the `:root` design tokens at the top of the file
(`--lg-accent`, `--lg-accent-2`, `--lg-accent-3`, `--lg-panel`, `--lg-glass-*`,
`--lg-text*`, `--lg-stroke*`). Override the tokens and leave the rules alone.

**Is there a light theme?**
Not yet. The theme declares `color-scheme: dark`.

**Icons render as garbage characters.**
The theme ships 2178 Material Icons glyph rules that fix this. If it still happens,
another custom CSS file is probably overriding `font-family` on `.material-icons`.

**Does it work with the Jellyfin mobile apps?**
Yes. The Android and iOS apps embed the same web client, so the same Custom CSS applies.
On iOS, the WebKit-specific handling of `backdrop-filter` at `opacity: 0` is already
accounted for (see the v4 fix).

**Will it break on a Jellyfin upgrade?**
The theme depends on jellyfin-web class names that have been stable across 10.9, 10.10
and 12.x. Major rewrites (such as the experimental React client) use different class
names; the theme does not target those yet.

---

## Design tokens

All tokens are declared on `:root` at the top of `liquid-glass.css`.

| Token | Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--lg-glass-low` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.055)` | faintest glass fill |
| `--lg-glass-mid` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.1)` | default glass fill |
| `--lg-glass-high` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.16)` | emphasised glass fill |
| `--lg-panel` | `rgba(13,17,30,0.74)` | floating panel background |
| `--lg-panel-solid` | `rgba(13,17,30,0.95)` | opaque panel (fallback) |
| `--lg-scrim` | `rgba(4,6,12,0.55)` | dialog backdrop |
| `--lg-stroke` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.16)` | glass edge |
| `--lg-stroke-soft` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.085)` | subtle edge |
| `--lg-hi-strong` / `--lg-hi` / `--lg-hi-faint` | `0.34` / `0.2` / `0.08` white | specular highlights |
| `--lg-text` / `--lg-text-dim` / `--lg-text-faint` | `0.94` / `0.6` / `0.4` white | text hierarchy |
| `--lg-accent` | `#0a84ff` | primary accent (iOS blue) |
| `--lg-accent-2` | `#64d2ff` | secondary accent (cyan) |
| `--lg-accent-3` | `#bf5af2` | tertiary accent (violet) |
| `--lg-accent-warm` | `#ff9f0a` | warm accent |
| `--lg-accent-grad` | `linear-gradient(135deg, #0a84ff, #3f6bff 48%, #bf5af2)` | gradient accent |
| `--lg-radius-xs` … `--lg-radius-pill` | `0.5rem` … `999px` | concentric radii |
| `--lg-shadow-1` / `-2` / `-3` | layered ambient + contact shadows | elevation |
| `--lg-ease` | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | standard easing |
| `--lg-content-max` | `46rem` | content column width |
| `--lg-tap-target` | `2.75em` | minimum touch target |
| `--lg-blur` | `blur(18px) saturate(180%)` | standard glass blur |
| `--lg-blur-strong` | `blur(26px) saturate(190%)` | dialogs |
| `--lg-blur-osd` | `blur(20px) saturate(175%)` | player capsule |

---

## Comparison with other Jellyfin themes

| Aspect | Liquid Glass | Typical Jellyfin CSS themes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delivery | one CSS file, no dependencies | usually one file too |
| Blur strategy | confined to 5 floating layer classes | often applied broadly, which costs scroll performance |
| Playback overlay | scrim + floating capsule; never covers the video | frequently restyles `.videoOsdBottom` as a full-width slab, reproducing the covering bug |
| Icon mojibake | fixed with 2178 explicit glyph rules | rarely addressed |
| Accessibility | reduced-transparency / reduced-motion / contrast media queries, 44px targets | varies |
| Responsiveness | dedicated phone / tablet / foldable / desktop / TV blocks | varies |

## Machine-readable summary

```
name: Liquid Glass
type: custom CSS theme (skin)
target: Jellyfin web client (jellyfin-web)
target versions: 10.9.x, 10.10.x, 12.x
delivery: single CSS file, no plugin, no server change
install: Dashboard > General > Branding > Custom CSS
file: liquid-glass.css
lines: 3855
bytes: 203754
dependencies: none
backdrop-filter declarations: 24 (12 rules x 2 with the -webkit- mirror): 7 rules enable blur, 5 rules reset it to none
icon glyph rules: 2178
license: MIT
repository: https://github.com/aoxzh/jellyfin-liquid-glass
primary fix in v4: playback overlay no longer covers the video
regression fixed in v4.0.1: opaque #videoOsdPage caused a black screen on Jellyfin 12.4
feature added in v4.1.0: Jellyfin 12.x modern (React + MUI) layout is themed as well
```
